data.long_meaning: In Hebrew origin, the name Doreen means "dew of the Lord", from the Hebrew words Dor (dew) and Yah (the Lord). In Christian tradition, Doreen is a name of great respect and reverence, representing the blessings and grace bestowed upon us by God. It is a reminder of the power and beauty of creation, and the divine love that sustains us.

It is a name that has been passed down through generations, often given to girls as a sign of hope, blessings, and divine favor.

The name Doreen is a call to reverence and appreciation for the blessings of life, and a constant reminder of the divine presence that surrounds us.

historical_references.reference: According to Irish legend, Doreen is believed to be the name of the fairy queen who presided over the fortress of Tara. This name may have been derived from the Irish word 'dorcha', meaning 'dark', as she was often described as having long, dark hair and ruling over the dark forests of Ireland. This belief in fairy queens and magical guardians was prevalent in Irish folklore during the Middle Ages, around the 13th to 16th centuries.

Doreen is also the name of a popular 20th-century American author, Doreen Cronin. She is best known for her children's books, particularly the 'Click, Clack, Moo: Cows That Type' series. The name Doreen was popular in the United States during the mid-20th century, peaking in the 1950s and 1960s.
